stem: Find the area of the triangle whose vertices are \((3, 8)\), \((-4, 2)\) and \((5, 1)\).
solution:
The area of triangle is given by
\[\Delta = \frac{1}{2}\begin{vmatrix} 3 & 8 & 1 \\ -4 & 2 & 1 \\ 5 & 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= \frac{1}{2}\left[3(2-1) - 8(-4-5) + 1(-4-10)\right]\]
\[= \frac{1}{2}(3 + 72 - 14) = \frac{61}{2}\]

stem: Find the equation of the line joining \(A(1, 3)\) and \(B(0, 0)\) using determinants and find \(k\) if \(D(k, 0)\) is a point such that area of triangle ABD is 3 sq units.
solution:
Let \(P(x, y)\) be any point on AB. Then, area of triangle ABP is zero (Why?). So
\[\frac{1}{2}\begin{vmatrix} 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 \\ x & y & 1 \end{vmatrix} = 0\]
This gives \(\frac{1}{2}(y - 3x) = 0\) or \(y = 3x\), which is the equation of required line AB.
Also, since the area of the triangle ABD is 3 sq. units, we have
\[\frac{1}{2}\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ k & 0 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = \pm 3\]
This gives, \(\frac{-3k}{2} = \pm 3\), i.e., \(k = \mp 2\).
